text.p: (a) Excludes acquisition expenses of $534,000 incurred primarily in connection with the Retek Distribution Corp. acquisition in the fourth quarter of 1996 and fully taxed at a 38 percent tax rate. (b) During the three months ended Dec. 31, 1996, the company recognized a $2.7 million deferred tax asset based upon anticipated future utilization of all of the remaining net operating loss carryforwards and research and development credit carryforwards primarily for Risk Data Corp. and also for Retek Distribution Corp., which resulted in a net income tax benefit of $2.3 million. This was a one-time tax benefit.

Revenues for the 12 months of 1996 were $53.8 million, an increase of 76 percent over the revenues of $30.7 million in the 12 months of 1995. Income before taxes was $5.8 million (after acquisition expenses of $1.2 million) for the 12 months of 1996 compared with $1.5 million for the 12 months of 1995.

Net income was $6.4 million (after acquisition expenses of $1.2 million and including a tax benefit of $608,000) for the 12 months of 1996 compared with $2.1 million (including the 1995 income tax benefit of $575,000). Earnings per share were 31 cents per share (after acquisition expenses of $1.2 million and including the income tax benefit of $608,000) or 21 cents per share (excluding acquisition expenses of $1.2 million and fully taxed) for the 12 months of 1996 compared with 13 cents per share (including the 1995 income tax benefit of $575,000) or 6 cents per share (excluding the 1995 tax benefit of $575,000 and fully taxed) for the 12 months of 1995.

(a) Excludes acquisition expenses of $515,000 incurred in connection with the acquisition of Retek, $563,000 incurred in connection with the acquisition of Risk Data Corp. and $99,000 for the terminated CRMA acquisition and fully taxed at a 38 percent tax rate. (b) During the 12 months ended Dec. 31, 1995, the company recognized a $1.7 million deferred tax asset based upon anticipated future utilization of all of the remaining net operating loss carryforwards and research and development credit carryforwards, which resulted in a net income tax benefit of $575,000. This was a one-time tax benefit. (c) During the 12 months ended Dec. 31, 1996, the company recognized a $2.7 million deferred tax asset based upon anticipated future utilization of all of the remaining net operating loss carryforwards and research and development credit carryforwards of Risk Data Corp. and Retek Distribution Corp., which resulted in a net income tax benefit of $608,000. This was a one-time tax benefit.
